science_value.rationale: Direct access to a classic polar PSR, impact-melt and regolith records, and one of the best-known Peaks of Eternal Light settings. High unique-sample potential.

thermal_stability.rationale: Polar surface temperatures are relatively stable, but the site sits beside cryogenic PSR terrain with extreme gradients over short distances.

crew_safety.rationale: Steep crater-rim slopes, shadow navigation, and intermittent direct-to-Earth geometry complicate aborts and surface operations.

data_maturity.rationale: Exceptionally dense LOLA coverage (5 m polar DEM used here), LROC NAC stereo, and LEND hydrogen mapping.

isru_water_ice.rationale: PSR access is excellent; LEND hydrogen anomalies and mapped cold traps make this a prime volatile-prospecting target.

shackleton_rim.psr_context: Mapped Shackleton PSR centroid is ~12.9 km away; equivalent-area edge is ~4.2 km from the rim point.

science_value.rationale: Polar highland stratigraphy, adjacent PSRs, and a well-studied Artemis candidate region with diverse impact and volatile processes.

thermal_stability.rationale: Stable polar environment with slightly more benign ridge exposure than the Shackleton rim, but still adjacent to cryogenic terrain.

crew_safety.rationale: Rolling highland terrain and PSR margins are manageable, and direct-to-Earth geometry is better than at the pole; relay coverage is still prudent.

data_maturity.rationale: Dense LOLA 30 m polar DEM used here, LROC stereo coverage, and dedicated Artemis III candidate-region studies.

isru_water_ice.rationale: Several mapped PSRs lie within a few kilometres of the ridge, giving excellent volatile-access potential.

nobile_connecting_ridge.psr_context: Nearest mapped PSR centroid is ~10.7 km away; equivalent-area edge is ~3.1 km from the ridge point.

science_value.rationale: Exposes deep SPA basin material and has Chang'e-4/Yutu-2 ground truth in the same crater; outstanding far-side crustal and volatile science.

thermal_stability.rationale: Normal equatorial far-side day/night cycle with a roughly 14-day night; large thermal swings for equipment and crews.

crew_safety.rationale: Broad, relatively flat basin floor is trafficable; the dominant operational risk is the lack of direct Earth visibility and reliance on a relay.

data_maturity.rationale: Global LOLA coverage, LROC imagery, and unique Chang'e-4 surface data; no high-resolution NASA NAC DTM at this exact point.

isru_water_ice.rationale: No polar PSR access. Any ice would be subsurface or in cold traps at higher latitude; unproven at this site.

science_value.rationale: A premier volcanic province with domes, sinuous rilles, and lava-tube skylights; exceptional for volcanology and subsurface access.

thermal_stability.rationale: Equatorial day/night cycle with large surface-temperature swings; lava tubes offer local shielding but are an engineering challenge.

crew_safety.rationale: Flat plains are interrupted by skylights, rilles, and boulder fields; subsurface operations add complexity.

data_maturity.rationale: LROC NAC DTM (2 m used here), Kaguya Terrain Camera, and M3 spectral coverage; no landed ground truth.

isru_water_ice.rationale: No polar PSR access; lava-tube cold traps are a possible but unverified volatile target.

science_value.rationale: The Moon's largest sinuous rille and Cobra Head vent, adjacent to young Aristarchus ejecta; outstanding volcanic and spectral science.

thermal_stability.rationale: Equatorial plateau with large day/night swings; deep rille walls create local thermal and lighting extremes.

crew_safety.rationale: Extreme relief, cliffs exceeding 1 km, and rille-edge hazards make landing and surface mobility difficult.

data_maturity.rationale: Global LOLA and LROC imagery, plus a 10 m Aristarchus DTM that stops just east of the exact site; a dedicated NAC DTM is missing.

isru_water_ice.rationale: No polar PSR access and no verified local volatile trap.

science_value.rationale: Unmatched ground truth, sample context, and operational heritage; scientifically mature rather than frontier, but ideal for validating terrain and planning algorithms.

thermal_stability.rationale: Equatorial valley with a 14-day day/night cycle; massif shadowing modifies local temperatures.

crew_safety.rationale: Well-characterised valley floor, benign trafficability, excellent Earth visibility, and extensive operational heritage.

data_maturity.rationale: Complete Apollo 17 surface photography, traverse profiles, soil mechanics, and a 5 m NAC DTM used here; the best-validated site in the set.

isru_water_ice.rationale: No polar PSR access and no verified local ice resource.
